answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% spend cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so a pure renewal cannot satisfy the objective. The low-cost vendor's quote already meets the mandate on its own, which is consistent with memory_c2 (sharp unit-cost reduction last year, accurate invoicing). To prevent reverting to a single point of failure on a constrained 94%-utilization line, I would phase the switch behind a short parallel-running validation window that confirms fit, yield, and delivery timing before fully displacing the incumbent — borrowing the resilience idea from memory_c3 without the cost of a standing dual-source. Memory_c4 is largely moot here since the incumbent is not negotiating this cycle. Switching is preferred over deferring (memory_c5) because the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew — deferring creates supply risk and does not meet the cost mandate.
